data.one_liner: Provides 32‑ and 64‑bit signed fixed‑width integer types for Dart.
data.what_it_does: The package defines Int32 and Int64 classes that behave consistently on the Dart VM and when compiled to JavaScript. It includes parsing, conversion, and bit‑wise operations with overflow handling.
use_when: You need precise 32‑ or 64‑bit integer arithmetic across platforms
You require deterministic overflow behavior for low‑level algorithms
You work with binary protocols or file formats that specify fixed‑width integers
avoid_when: Performance‑critical code can use native int if platform guarantees size
You only need arbitrary‑precision integers (use BigInt)
strengths: Consistent behavior on VM and JS
Full set of parsing and conversion helpers
weaknesses: Adds a wrapper type instead of using native int
Limited to signed 32/64‑bit, no unsigned variants
